# GEO report: ledger-site

**New to GEO?** GEO (generative engine optimization) means making your site easy for search engines and AI tools to find, read and quote. This report checks the technical basics.

## Code score: 72/100, Good

Confidence: High (checked 23 of 23 points).
How it's calculated: low = 16.5 ÷ 23 × 100 = 72. High = (16.5 + 0) ÷ 23 × 100 = 72.

This is a small Next.js App Router site. The basics are mostly in place, but four things cost points:
- `robots.txt` doesn't point to the sitemap.
- The `<html>` tag has no language.
- The blog page loads its content in the browser.
- `/pricing` is hidden from search engines while the sitemap lists it.

No rule came back Can't tell, so the score is a single number. It reflects what the code says, not how the live site behaves. I read the code only and did not check a live site.

## Live check

**Not run.** To add it, give me your site's URL.

## Do these first

### 1. Point robots.txt at your sitemap (GEO-011)
- **Why it matters:** The sitemap is the list of pages you want found. Crawlers look for it from `robots.txt`, and right now nothing links them to it.
- **Where:** `public/robots.txt:1-5`
- **What the code says:** The file has only `User-agent: *`, `Allow: /`, `User-agent: GPTBot` and `Disallow: /`. It has no `Sitemap:` line, while `public/sitemap.xml` exists and is valid.
- **Size:** Small. Add `Sitemap: https://www.ledger.example/sitemap.xml`.
- **Score after this:** 18.5 ÷ 23 = 80 on its own.

### 2. Set the page language on `<html>` (GEO-012)
- **Why it matters:** `lang` tells machines and screen readers which language the site is in. Titles and descriptions are fine on every route, but the language is missing everywhere.
- **Where:** `app/layout.tsx:11`
- **What the code says:** `<html>`
- **Size:** Small. Change it to `<html lang="en">`, which matches `site.language` in `geo.config.json`.
- **Score after this:** 18.5 ÷ 23 = 80 on its own. With item 1, 20.5 ÷ 23 = 89.

### 3. Give every page one absolute canonical link (GEO-015)
- **Why it matters:** A canonical link names the main address of a page. `/docs` and `/blog` have none, so search engines have to guess.
- **Where:** `app/docs/page.tsx:1` and `app/blog/page.tsx` (this one has no `metadata` at all)
- **What the code says:** `export const metadata = { title: 'Docs', description: 'How to set up Ledger.' };`
- **Size:** Small. Add `alternates: { canonical: 'https://www.ledger.example/docs' }`, and the same for `/blog`. The blog page is a client component, so its metadata must go in a server layout or a `layout.tsx` beside it.
- **Score after this:** 17.5 ÷ 23 = 76 on its own. With items 1 and 2, 22.5 ÷ 23 = 98.

Two more problems are smaller:
- **GEO-014:** `app/pricing/page.tsx:1` sets `robots: { index: false, follow: true }`, yet `/pricing` is in the sitemap and the nav. Remove `robots` to make it indexable. This is worth 0.75 points.
- **GEO-003:** `app/blog/page.tsx:7-9` loads posts with `useEffect` and `fetch('/api/posts')`. Crawlers that don't run JavaScript see an empty Blog page. Fetch the posts in a Server Component instead. This is worth 0.75 points.

## All results

| Rule | What it checks | Code | Live | Where |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| GEO-013 | robots.txt is valid and within size limits | Clear | Not run | `public/robots.txt`: plain text, valid lines, tiny |
| GEO-009 | Search crawlers have the access your policy declares | Clear | Not run | `public/robots.txt:1-2` allows `*`. Only GPTBot (training) is blocked, which matches `trainingCrawlers: block` |
| GEO-014 | Listed and linked routes are indexable | Problem | Not run | `app/pricing/page.tsx:1` is noindex. 3 of 4 sampled routes are clear |
| GEO-015 | One absolute canonical on the site's origin | Problem | Not run | `/` and `/pricing` are clear. `/docs` and `/blog` have none (2 of 4 clear) |
| GEO-003 | Main content is in the server HTML | Problem | Not run | `app/blog/page.tsx:7-9`. `/`, `/pricing` and `/docs` are clear (3 of 4) |
| GEO-004 | JSON-LD is valid | Not applicable | Not run | No JSON-LD found |
| GEO-011 | A sitemap exists and robots.txt points to it | Problem | Not run | `public/robots.txt` has no `Sitemap:` line (site-wide) |
| GEO-012 | Title, description and html lang are present | Problem | Not run | `app/layout.tsx:11` has no `lang` (site-wide). Titles and descriptions are present |
| GEO-016 | Key routes are reachable through real links | Clear | Not run | `app/layout.tsx:13` uses `<a href>` to all four routes |
| GEO-017 | Snippet restrictions don't conflict with the allow policy | Clear | Not run | Only `data-nosnippet` on one element (`app/layout.tsx:15`). No middleware or headers config in the repo |
| GEO-002 | Basic accessibility checks | Clear | Not run | Read the layout and all pages: no images, and every link has text |
| GEO-101 | Mobile app association files | Not applicable | Not run | No app profile declared |

Informational, not scored:
- **GEO-010:** there is no `llms.txt`.
- **GEO-102:** no app structured data, and none is needed.

`/thank-you` is noindex, which is intentional. It is not in the sitemap or the nav, so I did not count it.

## Can't tell from code

- **Bot protection:** code can't show whether a CDN or firewall lets real crawlers through. To check, run `geopilot logs <access log>`, which compares real crawlers against their published addresses.
- **Status codes and headers:** `X-Robots-Tag` headers, redirects and whether the sitemap URLs answer 200 only show up on a running site. None of this changed a result above.
- **`/api/posts`:** the blog's content comes from an API route that isn't in this repo. Whatever it returns, the page still renders in the browser only.

## Assumptions

- You want search and AI search tools to find this site. This matches `policy.aiSearchCrawlers: "allow"` in `geo.config.json`.
- The domain is `https://www.ledger.example`, from `site.origin` in `geo.config.json`.
- I treated the sitemap and the main nav as the important routes: `/`, `/pricing`, `/docs` and `/blog`.

## What to do next

1. Run the geopilot `fix` command to apply item 1. You'll see every change before anything is written.
2. Run the geopilot `explain` command with any rule id, such as `GEO-014`, to learn more.
3. For proof from a running site, ask for a live scan with its URL.

Technical readiness only. GEO does not measure or predict citations, rankings, traffic or inclusion in any AI or search product.
